analysis.one_liner: GAIL (India) Ltd runs the country's largest natural gas transmission pipeline network and trades gas, while also running petrochemical, LPG, and LNG businesses.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results are due on 30 October 2026, within the next two weeks. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) showed standalone PAT of ₹4,292 crore (up ~128% YoY) and consolidated PAT of ₹4,671 crore (up ~96% YoY), driven largely by a record, one-off LPG segment profit. Separately, the regulator (PNGRB) approved only a 12% tariff hike for GAIL's main gas pipeline (to ₹65.69/MMBtu versus the ₹78.72 GAIL had sought), which pulled the stock down 4-6% on the news.
analysis.plain_terms: GAIL moves gas through pipelines across India and sells it, while also running petrochemical and LPG businesses on the side. The big profit jump investors are reading about came mostly from a temporary spike in LPG prices, which management itself said on the earnings call would not repeat - the underlying gas transmission business was roughly flat. So the question isn't whether GAIL made money last quarter, it did, it's whether that level of profit can continue once LPG prices normalize and the chronically loss-making petrochemical unit actually reaches the breakeven management has promised.
analysis.quarters: Standalone revenue/EBITDA/PAT (₹ crore) over the last five quarters: Q1 FY26 34,769/3,334/1,886; Q2 FY26 35,008/3,191/2,217; Q3 FY26 34,051/2,655/1,603; Q4 FY26 34,773/1,152/1,262; Q1 FY27 38,953/6,376/4,292. Note the standalone PAT figure (₹4,292 cr) differs from the consolidated figure (₹4,671 cr) by about ₹379 crore - both are correct, just different consolidation bases, and news outlets have mixed them up. Management flagged the LPG segment's record profit (PBT ₹772 crore, up from ₹144 crore) as driven by a temporary Middle East-linked price spike and explicitly said it is not sustainable. Petrochemical losses narrowed sharply to an EBITDA loss of ₹11 crore from ₹390 crore the prior quarter, with management guiding to breakeven during FY27. Gas transmission volumes were about 122.4 MMSCMD, roughly flat YoY and still below FY25's ~127 MMSCMD peak.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 24.7% from its July 2024 peak of ₹223.23 to the current ₹168.1, inside a 52-week range of ₹135-181. This is a genuine price pullback, not a corporate-action artifact - GAIL's five stock splits all happened between 2008 and 2022, well before this peak, so both the peak and current price are already on a consistent split-adjusted basis. Zooming out, GAIL has strongly outperformed over longer horizons: +42.4% over 3 years versus Nifty's +16.8% and peer Petronet's +41.0%, and +93.9% over 5 years versus Nifty's +25.3% and Petronet's +54.1%. The 1-year and 3-month returns are roughly flat to slightly negative, but still ahead of the Nifty's declines over the same periods.
analysis.valuation_read: At ~11.2x trailing P/E and ~1.24x P/B, GAIL looks statistically cheap for a dominant gas infrastructure business with government backing. Why it looks cheap: ROE (8.71% TTM) and ROCE (9.67% TTM) have both fallen well below their own 10-year averages (around 13% and a prior peak of 23% in FY2022 respectively), as the earlier boom in gas trading and transmission margins has normalized. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether those returns recover - through higher pipeline tariffs, petrochemical breakeven, or volume growth - or whether today's lower profitability is simply the new baseline the market is correctly pricing in.
analysis.growth_read: More price/margin-led than volume-led at present. Core gas transmission volumes are roughly flat year-on-year at about 122.4 MMSCMD and still below FY25's ~127 MMSCMD peak, with FY27 guidance of only ~123 MMSCMD - a modest ask, not a growth story. The large profit jump this quarter came from a temporary spike in LPG prices and narrower petrochemical losses, not from moving or selling more gas.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk looks low: debt-to-equity has stayed around 0.25-0.28x for the past three years, and total debt of ₹16,793 crore (June 2026) is small relative to quarterly profits running into the thousands of crores. The real concern is business risk, not balance-sheet risk - the petrochemical segment remains structurally loss-making (though losses are narrowing), and the recent profit beat leaned on a one-off LPG price spike that management itself said would not repeat. There is also a disputed excise duty demand of roughly ₹3,799 crore (with interest) under appeal; its eventual resolution is Not verified - check on Screener or company filings for provisioning status.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the Government of India, holding a steady ~51.8-51.9% for the past two years, with no pledging (government holdings are not pledged, consistent with a standard PSU structure). Foreign institutional holding has risen from about 13.0% (March 2026) to roughly 16.6% (September 2026), suggesting renewed foreign buying, while domestic institutional holding has fallen from about 20.5% to 17.9% over the same stretch - domestic institutions appear to have sold into that foreign buying. A secondary source names LIC as a top non-promoter holder at roughly 8.6%, but this figure is Not verified - check on Screener directly for current large shareholders.
strengths: Debt-to-equity of only about 0.25-0.28x, among the least leveraged balance sheets in the sector.
Consolidated PAT of ₹4,671 crore in Q1 FY27, up 96% YoY, supporting a 3.27% dividend yield at a payout ratio of roughly 48% of profit.
5-year total return of 93.85%, well ahead of the Nifty's 25.27% and peer Petronet's 54.13% over the same period.
Petrochemical segment losses narrowed to an EBITDA loss of just ₹11 crore in Q1 FY27, down from a ₹390 crore loss the prior quarter, with management guiding to breakeven during FY27.
watchpoints: Q1 FY27's profit jump relied heavily on a record LPG segment result (PBT ₹772 crore) that management explicitly called unsustainable, tied to a temporary Middle East supply disruption.

ROE (8.71% TTM) and ROCE (9.67% TTM) both sit well below their 10-year averages, and the regulator capped GAIL's latest pipeline tariff hike at 12% (to ₹65.69/MMBtu) against a 34% ask (₹78.72), with the next tariff review not due until April 2028.
Core gas transmission volumes (~122.4 MMSCMD) remain below the FY25 peak of ~127 MMSCMD, and FY27 guidance of ~123 MMSCMD implies only modest recovery.
A disputed excise duty demand of about ₹3,799 crore (with interest) remains under appeal, with provisioning status Not verified - check on Screener or company filings.
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due 30 October 2026 will show whether the LPG-driven profit spike unwinds as management warned and whether petrochemical losses keep narrowing toward the guided FY27 breakeven - together these will reveal whether Q1 FY27's surge was a one-off or the start of a durable recovery.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly financials and shareholding pattern were cross-checked directly against Screener.in. Standalone (₹4,292 cr) and consolidated (₹4,671 cr) Q1 FY27 PAT figures differ by about ₹379 crore across news sources due to consolidation basis, not error - both are used above with that basis noted. Could not independently verify: Konkan LNG's reported conversion to a wholly-owned subsidiary (single unconfirmed source), LIC's exact shareholding (~8.6%, one secondary source only), AGM ordinal sequence numbering (sources disagreed, though dates were consistent), and GAIL's historical long-term average P/E (not available from the source checked).
